reading: The US market ROSE ~21% on the OUTBREAK of WWII (peak 13.17, mid-Sept) -- the 'war boom': orders for neutral American industry. It priced the war it could PROFIT from, not war-as-catastrophe.
Eight months of relative calm. The market did NOT price the possibility that France might fall -- the classic anticipation gap.
The fall of France repriced the market violently -- a systemic threat: Germany dominant in Europe, the US position endangered, entry looming. A surprise (the speed shocked it), not a priced-in event.
One of the sharpest US crashes -- the war had changed character from distant boom to systemic danger.
